$comment: The rename table (#31): Reactor's member, parameter, modifier, type and factory names and Isotope's Avalonia names for them.
Read by the library's tests (RenameTableTests) and by the Reactor migration analyzer (#33). Format: tools/naming/README.md.

members.note: Label and ContentElement are one Content (object?): a string or an element, as Avalonia's ContentControl.Content.
See Label.
IsChecked is the bool? value; a three-state box sets IsThreeState.
One callback, Action<bool?>. The factory CheckBox still takes an Action<bool>, called for checked and unchecked only.
Now an Action<bool?> on the record (it was Action<bool>); the CheckBox factory adapts an Action<bool>.
Label and ContentElement are one Content (object?): a string or an element.
See Label.
Now a bool? (it was bool), holding the three-state value too.

Now an Action<bool?> on the record (it was Action<bool>); the ToggleButton factory adapts an Action<bool>.

Now an object? (it was string): a string or an element.
Content and ContentElement are one Content (object?).

Upstream's ScrollView is Avalonia's ScrollViewer here, and its ContentOrientation (WinUI's ScrollingContentOrientation) is the scroll bar visibilities: Vertical, ScrollView's default, is a Disabled horizontal scroll bar; Horizontal a Disabled vertical one; Both leaves both Auto; None disables both.
Now an object? (it was string): a string or an element.
Header and HeaderContent are one Header (object?): a string or an element.
No Avalonia counterpart: AutoCompleteBox has no query-submitted event (this is Enter in the box).
No exact counterpart: Avalonia's SelectionChanged also fires when typed text matches a suggestion; this reports the user's picks only.
GridDefinition(Columns, Rows) is two GridSize[] members, as Avalonia's ColumnDefinitions and RowDefinitions; GridDefinition is gone (see types).
No exact counterpart: Avalonia's MenuItem takes one gesture (HotKey and InputGesture, both written from the first); upstream's Command.Accelerator shares the type.
No single counterpart: written as the item's ToolTip.Tip and AutomationProperties.HelpText.
No Avalonia counterpart: TreeView has no item-invoked event (this is a tap on an item, or Enter or Space on it).
No Avalonia event on TreeView: raised from TreeViewItem's Expanded, after the item expands (WinUI's Expanding comes before).
No Avalonia counterpart: Avalonia's text has no blocks. Each paragraph is a Span of its inlines, with a LineBreak between paragraphs; Inlines is Avalonia's member (#65).
WinUI's is an int in 1/1000 em; Avalonia's LetterSpacing is a double in DIPs (CharacterSpacing * FontSize / 1000).
Now Avalonia's TextDecorationCollection (it was WinUI's TextDecorations flags): Avalonia.Media.TextDecorations.Underline or .Strikethrough, or .Underline() and .Strikethrough().
Now Avalonia's FontFamily (it was a string), which a string converts to.
Avalonia has FontWeight only: IsBold = true is FontWeight = FontWeight.Bold, or .Bold().
Avalonia has FontStyle only: IsItalic = true is FontStyle = FontStyle.Italic, or .Italic().
Avalonia has TextDecorations only: IsStrikethrough = true is TextDecorations = Avalonia.Media.TextDecorations.Strikethrough, or .Strikethrough().

parameters.note: Avalonia's NumericUpDown has no header (Reactor's NumberBox took it third): put a TextBlock label beside it; PlaceholderText is the text shown while it is empty (#68).

modifiers.note: Avalonia's Layoutable.HorizontalAlignment, which upstream also has as an alias of HAlign (#46).
Avalonia's Layoutable.VerticalAlignment, which upstream also has as an alias of VAlign (#46).
No modifier: set the record's Minimum and Maximum, NumericUpDown(value, onValueChanged) with { Minimum = min, Maximum = max } (#68).
No modifier: Avalonia's NumericUpDown shows its spinner by default (ShowButtonSpinner, null keeps it); with { ShowButtonSpinner = false } hides it, and Reactor's placement has no counterpart (#68).
No counterpart in the same unit: WinUI's CharacterSpacing is in 1/1000 em, Avalonia's LetterSpacing in DIPs. Use .LetterSpacing(spacing * fontSize / 1000) (#65).
No Avalonia counterpart by name: Avalonia sets a ControlTheme through Theme. This sets one by resource key (a WinUI style key), with Isotope's type ramp as the fallback; text blocks only (#44).

types.note: Removed with GridElement.Definition: pass the GridSize[] columns and rows to GridElement or Grid(...); strings become tracks through GridSize.Parse (Array.ConvertAll(columns, GridSize.Parse)).
WinUI's TabView is Avalonia's TabControl (#46).
A tab is Avalonia's TabItem (#46).
WinUI's NumberBox is Avalonia's NumericUpDown (#46).
WinUI's AutoSuggestBox is Avalonia's AutoCompleteBox (#46).
Avalonia's ProgressBar (#46).
Avalonia's StackPanel (#46); its factories, VStack and HStack, keep their names.
WinUI's MenuBar is Avalonia's Menu (#46); its factory, MenuBar, keeps its name.
A top-level menu is an Avalonia MenuItem, as every menu item is. MenuItemData would name only this one of the five item records, while MenuItem(...) builds a MenuFlyoutItemData (#46).

Avalonia's name would be MenuFlyoutElement, but that is another Reactor record (a target with a menu, from Reactor's MenuFlyout(target, items), not in Isotope yet): the rename would give a Reactor name another meaning, and the migration would leave its uses unflagged (#46).
Upstream's ScrollView is Avalonia's ScrollViewer (#43).
A node is Avalonia's TreeViewItem (#43): Header and Items for Content and Children.
Isotope's FlexPanel, over Reactor's port of Yoga, is not an Avalonia control: Reactor's name stays (#46).
Avalonia's MenuItem is every kind of menu item, and five Reactor item records map to it; the Reactor name says which kind (#46).

WinUI's RichTextBlock is Avalonia's SelectableTextBlock (#65).
Avalonia's Inline (#65). Inlines are elements, so a key and the text modifiers apply to them.
Avalonia's Run (#65).
Avalonia's LineBreak (#65).
Avalonia's InlineUIContainer (#65). Its Child is an element; Reactor's Factory (a native control) has no counterpart.
No Avalonia counterpart: Avalonia's text has no paragraphs (blocks). A paragraph is a Span of its inlines on a line of its own (#65).

Avalonia's name, Menu, is Reactor's factory for a top-level menu (MenuBar(Menu("File", ...))); renaming both would give Reactor's Menu another meaning (#46). The record is MenuElement.
A top-level menu is an Avalonia MenuItem, but MenuItem(...) is Reactor's factory for a menu's items (#46).
A submenu is an Avalonia MenuItem, but MenuItem(...) is Reactor's factory for a plain item; the Reactor name says which kind (#46).
A check-mark item is an Avalonia MenuItem (ToggleType CheckBox), but MenuItem(...) is Reactor's factory for a plain item; the Reactor name says which kind (#46).
A radio item is an Avalonia MenuItem (ToggleType Radio), but MenuItem(...) is Reactor's factory for a plain item; the Reactor name says which kind (#46).
